findings.visible_symptom: Tile id 6 must be NE+SE land (weights 2+4) with NW and SW water. The NW quadrant (x0-7, y0-7) is painted land green #72b36c instead of water navy #254767; the file is byte-identical to tile-7 (NW+NE+SE). Everywhere tile 6 is placed, its NW corner shows land while the three tiles sharing that vertex show water, so the shoreline grows a square green stub into water at that vertex: a broken material join.
contextual_evidence: coverage-1x.png: NW quadrants of cells (row0,col3) px [48,0,8,8], (row2,col1) px [16,32,8,8], (row6,col5) px [80,96,8,8], (row7,col3) px [48,112,8,8], (row7,col5) px [80,112,8,8] are uniformly #72b36c where the vertex grid value is 0 (water). Clearest case: (row0,col3) sits right of cell (row0,col2) = tile 0 (all water): a green 8x8 block attached to open water.
coverage-3x.png: same five cells at 24x24 quadrants [144,0], [48,96], [240,288], [144,336], [240,336].

island-1x.png: cells (row1,col0) px [0,16,8,8] and (row2,col0) px [0,32,8,8] green where the west vertex column is all 0; pixl_asset_check shows the green component bbox [0,8,56,56] reaching x=0 although the authored island's land never touches the canvas edge (expected green bbox [8,8,56,56]).

island-3x.png and island-3x-destination.png (screenshot approx [36,281]-[60,305] and [36,329]-[60,353]): two green stubs visibly protrude left from the island's west shore into water; the island's east shore, which uses tile 9 / tile 11 / tile 13, is straight. The asymmetry is visible at 1x in island-1x.png and obvious at 3x.

All other 15 tiles match the contract in every placement: audit of every quadrant of every cell in both neighborhoods at 1x and 3x found mismatches only in tile-6 placements (5 in shoreline, 2 in island).
findings.mechanical_status: The consumer check passes (source, mapping and screenshot pixel checks) because the mapping and compositing of the bytes are correct; the fault is inside the authored bytes of member.6, which the pixel checks faithfully reproduce.
findings.likely_correction: Repaint only the NW quadrant of tile-6.png (x0-7, y0-7, 64 px) to navy #254767, giving green bbox [0,0,16,16] minus NW/SW, i.e. 128 green / 128 navy with navy in NW and SW. Produce it as a successor member for member.6.output; do not change src/terrain.ts, the corner order, or any neighborhood grid.
findings.preservation_scope: members 0-5 and 7-15 unchanged (tile-7.png keeps its current bytes; its same_bytes link to member.6 is expected to disappear). Both neighborhood definitions, tile_size, background, sampling and the destination config are unchanged.

findings.mechanical_status: All 58 pixel checks, 12 source checks and 244 clock checks pass: the renderer placed each 16x16 rect correctly at its pivot/anchor, honored the uneven durations, wrapped the loop twice and clamped the one-shot. The planted-floor failure is in the authored pixels, which a correct renderer reproduces exactly.

Changing pose-2's pivot in src to [8,16] would also realign the feet, but the brief fixes pivots at [8,14] and src must stay unchanged, so the pixel correction is the right one. Optionally, as a separate artistic revision, give pose-2 a distinct arm pose so the 4-pose cycle is not A-B-A-B.

controlled_faults_note: README.md says the fixture may contain two controlled pixel faults. From the pixels, exactly two source anomalies were found: tile-6.png NW quadrant (F1) and frame-2.png 2 px vertical translation (F2). No other member deviates from the corner contract or the shared ground line. This is an observation from the bytes, not knowledge of how the fixture was prepared.
mechanical_vs_visual: Separation statement: the consumer execution proves only what its checks implement: exact member bytes were served and composited, tile ids map to the vertex grids under NW=1/NE=2/SE=4/SW=8, each sprite rect was placed at pivot [8,14] on anchor [20,28] at 1x and 3x, authored durations drove observed transitions, the loop wrapped twice and the one-shot clamped. Both domains pass those checks. Visual continuity is a separate judgment made here from the actual captured pixels: the terrain fails the material-join intent at every tile-6 placement (F1), and the animation fails the planted-floor intent during pose-2 (F2). A mechanical pass therefore coexists with two visual continuity defects. Timing samples establish observed playback; stills do not establish subjective live viewing and no such viewing is claimed. No artistic acceptance, human acceptance or engine acceptance beyond this browser fixture is asserted.

limitations: Visual judgments rest on captured PNG stills at 1x and 3x plus sampled playback timing; no continuous video and no subjective live viewing by a human.

The quadrant audit and feet/head measurements were made with an ad-hoc Pillow script run inline (not retained as a file) and with pixl_asset_check color regions; pixl_asset_check rejected an x,y,w,h region syntax ('regions: invalid color'), so measurements used color-keyed component boxes instead.
pixl_consumer_execute's checks are the fixed browser profile's checks; they do not qualify another engine, seam quality or art quality.
The island neighborhood does not exercise tile ids 0, 5, 10 and 15; those are covered only by the mixed shoreline.
The family's q.continuity (visual) and q.destination (live) criteria remain status unperformed in state by design of this assignment; this file records specialist findings, not retained verdicts.
Real generated art, CF-09 revision and human acceptance remain open and were not attempted.
